questions.q: Per this lesson, why can two individually well-tested changes from different teams still cause a problem once deployed to the same org?
options: Because one of the two changes must have been poorly tested
Because a metadata conflict can occur when two independently developed changes interact badly together, even though neither is wrong on its own, simply because nobody coordinated them
Because Salesforce only allows one team to deploy per release
Because metadata conflicts only happen with Apex code, never with declarative changes
questions.explain: A metadata conflict is specifically about interaction, not individual correctness -- two reasonable changes can still break each other if nobody coordinated them across teams.

questions.q: What does a hub-and-spoke multi-org model look like, per this lesson?
options: A single org shared by every business unit with no separation at all
A sandbox refresh schedule, unrelated to org topology
A model where every team gets a fully independent org with zero integration between them
A central hub org for shared capabilities and data, with separate business-unit-specific spoke orgs integrated back to the hub
questions.explain: Hub-and-spoke keeps a central hub for cross-cutting capabilities while giving business units their own spoke orgs, integrated back to the hub -- a middle ground between one shared org and fully separate orgs.

questions.q: What trade-off does this lesson describe for giving each business unit its own separate Salesforce org?
options: It has no trade-offs at all -- it is strictly better in every case
It is only available to organizations with fewer than ten users
It reduces cross-team metadata conflict by removing the shared environment, but fragments reporting and duplicates administrative overhead since each org needs its own governance and admins
It eliminates the need for any governance model whatsoever
questions.explain: Separate orgs reduce the coordination problem created by a shared environment, but at the real cost of fragmented cross-business reporting and duplicated governance and admin overhead.

questions.q: What is an unlocked package, as described in this lesson?
options: A Salesforce DX packaging format that lets a team build and version its own metadata as a distinct, trackable unit within a shared org
A sandbox type with no data storage limit
A tool that automatically resolves all metadata conflicts between teams
A feature that merges every team's metadata into one undifferentiated pool
questions.explain: Unlocked packages give teams clearer ownership boundaries and visibility into what a given release changes, which reduces (without eliminating) how often conflicts happen inside a shared org.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does org-topology choice (single org, business-unit orgs, hub-and-spoke) belong at the strategic governance layer rather than being left to whichever team asks first?
options: Because the right choice depends on how much business units genuinely need to share data and process versus independence -- a decision with organization-wide consequences, not a single team's call
Because org topology has no real consequences either way
Because Salesforce technical support makes this decision automatically
Because only developers are qualified to choose an org topology
questions.explain: Org topology is a structural, organization-wide trade-off between shared visibility and team independence, which is exactly the kind of decision this course's Lesson 3 assigns to the strategic governance layer rather than ad hoc team requests.
